citations.narrative:
The facility did not have complete acquisition records for one American bison and two cows. In addition, disposition
records were not completed in full for one zebra, one yak, sixteen goats, two alpacas, and one llama. While the records
included some of the essential components, the missing required information varied (dates of acquisition/disposition,
names, addresses, driver’s license/license information and state), resulting in incomplete records for each animal.
Acquisition and disposition records, including offspring born at the facility, are necessary to accurately track and identify
animals being used in regulated activities, as well as aid in the detection of movement of animals upon relocation to a new
site. The licensee shall make, keep, and maintain records of acquisition/disposition of all animals that fully and correctly
disclose the required information, as outlined in this section.
Correct by October 31, 2026.

citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
The licensee has not submitted a written itinerary for events involving overnight stays since September 2025. During this
inspection, the licensee stated overnight travel with the regulated animals has occurred during the 2026 calendar year as
well. While the licensee believed their itineraries were previously submitted by a facility representative, APHIS officials
explained none have been provided since last year.
Submitting an itinerary ensures that Animal Care is aware of regulated animal movement and exhibition within the
country, and allows for inspections to be completed in accordance with the AWA when animals are away from the home
site. Traveling exhibitors must submit an itinerary to APHIS no fewer than 2 days in advance of any travel and shall
contain complete and accurate information concerning the whereabouts of any animal intended for exhibition at any
location other than the person's approved site.
Correct by October 14, 2026.

Three outdoor enclosures housing a total of four water buffalo, nine cows, one zebu, and one camel were excessively
soiled and muddy, with standing water present. Although the recent occurrence of rainfall increased the amount of water
exposure for these enclosures, there were no dry areas available for the animals to access their respective food troughs
and water receptacles without either standing or wading through the mud. In addition, the enclosure housing one camel
had mud that encompassed most of the sheltered housing area, with the animal's body also muddied. While the licensee
stated the camel enjoys rolling around in the mud, APHIS officials discussed concern of the limited dry areas of ground
near the shelter.
Failure to provide adequate drainage can result in excessively muddy conditions that may be hazardous or result in
discomfort or adverse impact, especially during inclement weather. The facility shall have a suitable method to rapidly
eliminate excess water from the enclosures.
Correct by October 18, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee and facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
